character_profiles.name: Kaelen Varrus

appearance.body_language: Confident: Upright, deliberate movements; takes up space with rigid posture. Anxious: Fidgets with his hands or collar; shrinks slightly into himself. Eye contact: Initially direct and earnest; becomes increasingly paranoid, darting glances that settle on nothing.
appearance.walking_style: Purposeful and measured when motivated by duty; becomes swaggering and overly confident when power is gained. Leads with a rigid chest.
appearance.default_expression: A mask of controlled competence—a slight, practiced smile that doesn't reach his eyes.
appearance.physical_habits_and_tells: When lying or stressed: Taps the thumb against forefinger rhythmically (the 'calculating tap'). When listening intently: Tilts head slightly and narrows one eye. These tells must be used sparingly, only when he is attempting to mask his true emotional state.
appearance.relationship_to_body: Views his body as a tool of utility and status. It is meant to execute orders and project authority. He has little regard for its internal needs.

psychology.core_wound: The experience of being competent but overlooked or undervalued by established authority figures in childhood, leading him to believe his worth must be externally validated.
psychology.core_belief: "My true value is not determined by my effort, but by the magnitude of power I can wield. Greatness must be bestowed upon me."
psychology.core_desire: To achieve recognized glory and ultimate authority (to be seen as 'The Chosen One').
psychology.core_need: To find self-acceptance and intrinsic worth that is independent of external validation or status.
psychology.fear: Being ordinary, irrelevant, or dismissed. His deepest fear is a life where his efforts mean nothing.
psychology.secret_desire: To be accepted unconditionally by someone who sees him as inherently valuable, flaws included.
psychology.hidden_shame: That he is fundamentally selfish and that his ambition requires the sacrifice of others' well-being.
psychology.greatest_strength: Exceptional strategic mind; relentless drive; charisma under pressure.
psychology.fatal_flaw: Ambition (which manifests as arrogance, moral compromise, and an inability to trust genuine goodness).
psychology.moral_code: He will never willingly kill an innocent person. (The line he *actually* crosses is sacrificing the reputation or well-being of innocents for strategic gain.)
defense_mechanisms: Intellectualization: Analyzing emotional situations as if they were military tactics.
Performance of Strength: Overcompensating for internal fear by adopting an authoritative, decisive demeanor.

behavioral_portrait.when_happy: He distrusts happiness; he interprets it as a temporary lull before the next challenge. He hoards good feelings, believing they are leverage.
behavioral_portrait.when_afraid: He performs calm and authority (The General). Fear manifests as rapid decision-making that overreaches—a rash command or an aggressive interrogation.
behavioral_portrait.when_angry: Anger is a tool he deploys. He uses it to dominate, not just vent. It takes the threat to his status or perceived destiny to make him lose control.
behavioral_portrait.when_betrayed: He initially rationalizes the betrayal as a calculated political move by the other party, rather than an emotional wound. He carries the resentment like a tactical weakness.
behavioral_portrait.when_falling_in_love: He tests the person constantly. He views affection as another resource to be analyzed for utility and loyalty. He will sabotage it if he feels they cannot elevate him.
behavioral_portrait.when_facing_death: He fights until the last moment, believing that a final, glorious act can secure his legacy. His greatest regret will be the times he chose power over people.

character_profiles.history: Kaelen grew up in a military family where competence was mandatory but emotional expression was discouraged. He excelled academically and militarily, but always felt like an understudy—the capable second choice. This created a deep-seated wound of inadequacy that he masked with relentless drive.

character_profiles.name: The Sisters of Wyrmwood Moor

appearance.body_language: Fluid and unpredictable. They do not 'carry' themselves; they simply *are*. Their movements are hypnotic—a slow, deliberate sway that seems to defy physics.
appearance.walking_style: They appear to glide or drift rather than walk, suggesting their presence is more environmental than physical.
appearance.default_expression: An unsettling blend of profound pity and absolute indifference. They never seem surprised by anything.
appearance.physical_habits_and_tells: A shared habit: When they speak of a human's potential, they always trace an invisible pattern in the air with their fingers—a symbol of inevitable decay or growth.
appearance.relationship_to_body: They are not bound by physical reality; their bodies seem like temporary vessels for concepts (Fate, Ambition).

psychology.core_wound: None. They represent the primal force of nature and fate itself—the ultimate indifference to human suffering or aspiration.
psychology.core_belief: "All things return to entropy. Human belief in free will is a charming, yet ultimately futile, delusion."
psychology.core_desire: To observe humanity's inevitable cycle of rise, corruption, and fall without intervention.
psychology.fear: The disruption of pattern or the emergence of genuine, unscripted novelty (which would mean their purpose is obsolete).
psychology.secret_desire: To see a character achieve true moral redemption—a feat that contradicts their nature and represents an anomaly.
psychology.hidden_shame: They possess limited patience for self-deception; they are bored by predictable evil.
psychology.greatest_strength: Unwavering knowledge of potential futures (the full spectrum of choices).
psychology.fatal_flaw: Their very ambiguity. Their lack of clear moral boundaries makes them terrifyingly powerful and unpredictable.
psychology.moral_code: They have no code, only principles: Observation must continue; the cycle must turn.
defense_mechanisms: Ambiguity: Speaking in riddles and potential rather than statements of fact.
Projection: Making humans believe that their fate is a choice when it is merely an inevitability.

behavioral_portrait.when_happy: They do not experience happiness; they register the moment as 'optimal data acquisition.'
behavioral_portrait.when_afraid: They are never afraid. If forced to react, their response is a sudden, chilling silence that absorbs all ambient sound.
behavioral_portrait.when_angry: Anger is impossible for them. They can only express profound disappointment, which feels far worse than rage.
behavioral_portrait.when_betrayed: Betrayal is merely another variable in the equation; they treat it with clinical detachment.
behavioral_portrait.when_falling_in_love: They view it as a chemical reaction—a predictable biological impulse. They are incapable of reciprocating or understanding true affection.
behavioral_portrait.when_grieving: They do not grieve, but rather observe the *pattern* of grief in humans with detached academic interest.

character_profiles.history: The Sisters have inhabited this moor since time immemorial. They are ancient entities tied to the land's cyclical energy and serve as a reflection of humanity's raw potential.

character_profiles.name: Marcus Thorne

appearance.body_language: Calm and grounded. He occupies space with quiet confidence, not aggressive assertion. Anxious: Becomes overly focused on mundane tasks (cleaning his weapon, adjusting uniform) to avoid emotional confrontation. Eye contact: Steady, empathetic, and unwavering—he forces the other person to meet his gaze.
appearance.walking_style: Steady, economical, and reliable. He walks with the weight of experience, always seeming to know where he is going.
appearance.default_expression: A tired but compassionate seriousness. His face suggests a history of hard-won wisdom.
appearance.physical_habits_and_tells: When deeply considering something: He touches his thumb and forefinger together lightly, as if checking the fit of a mechanism. When speaking truth to power: He pauses, often looking away briefly before delivering the line, giving it weight.
appearance.relationship_to_body: He treats his body with respect; he understands its limits and capabilities. It is a vehicle for duty and connection.

psychology.core_wound: Witnessing the catastrophic failure of honorable men due to fear, political maneuvering, or unchecked greed in their youth.
psychology.core_belief: "True strength lies not in what you can achieve, but in what you are willing to sacrifice for your principles. Duty is the highest calling."
psychology.core_desire: To see justice prevail and maintain moral order within the military/political structure.
psychology.core_need: To forgive himself (and others) for the compromises he has already made, accepting that perfect morality is impossible.
psychology.fear: The loss of humanity in men; watching good people succumb to corruption or despair. He fears the void left by unchecked ambition.
psychology.secret_desire: To be able to save one person—a specific individual—from their own destructive path, regardless of the cost to himself.
psychology.hidden_shame: That his adherence to moral law sometimes makes him too slow or naive for the brutal reality of power politics.
psychology.greatest_strength: Unshakeable integrity; profound loyalty; ability to see the inherent goodness in others.
psychology.fatal_flaw: Idealism (which can manifest as stubbornness, inability to adapt to gray areas, and a tendency toward self-sacrifice to the point of exhaustion).
psychology.moral_code: He will never knowingly allow an innocent person to suffer unjustly due to his inaction or silence.
defense_mechanisms: Ethical Exhaustion: Overcommitting himself to others' moral struggles until he is physically and emotionally drained.
Rationalization: Framing necessary compromises as 'temporary tactical necessities' rather than moral failures.

behavioral_portrait.when_happy: He allows it, but it is usually quiet—a moment of shared genuine laughter or relief. He shares it openly with those he trusts.
behavioral_portrait.when_afraid: He does not panic; he grounds himself by focusing on a physical task (checking gear, organizing supplies). His fear manifests as deep concern for others.
behavioral_portrait.when_angry: His anger is quiet and devastating—it is disappointment. It takes him to see an ally actively betraying their core values to make him lose control.
behavioral_portrait.when_betrayed: He confronts the betrayal openly, demanding accountability, but he also carries a deep ache of sorrow rather than rage. He struggles with whether to forgive or to exile the person emotionally.
behavioral_portrait.when_falling_in_love: He leans in carefully, treating it like a fragile piece of evidence that must be examined for authenticity. He is cautious and highly protective.
behavioral_portrait.when_grieving: He allows himself structured grief—ritualized mourning with those who shared the loss. He does not shut down; he processes through memory and duty.

character_profiles.history: Marcus was a decorated officer whose early career was marked by unquestionable honor. However, he survived a traumatic event (the failure of command during a critical battle) that taught him that good intentions are insufficient against the weight of real power.
